items.gloss_md: Browser and download hub of the University of California Santa Cruz that serves TCGA, GDC and GTEx data as one ready matrix per data type.
items.body_md:
- URL: <https://xenabrowser.net>; data are organised in hubs, e.g. the **GDC hub** (re-served GDC data such as `TCGA-PAAD.star_counts.tsv.gz`, `star_fpkm`, `clinical`, `survival`) and the **TOIL hub** (TCGA and GTEx recomputed with one pipeline).
- Values are delivered on a log2(x + 1) scale (counts, FPKM, TPM), rows are Ensembl ids; a separate *probemap* (e.g. `gencode.v36.annotation.gtf.gene.probemap`) maps ids to gene symbols.
- Advantage over the GDC portal: one matrix instead of one file per sample, no manifest, no registration.

items.gloss_md: The NCI portal that holds TCGA, CPTAC and other NCI programmes, re-processed with harmonised pipelines and served per file through a web portal and an API.
items.body_md:
- URL: <https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov>; programmatic access via the GDC API (file and case queries) or the gdc-client with a manifest.
- RNA-seq is harmonised: STAR alignment against GRCh38 with GENCODE v36 annotation, one *STAR gene-count* file per sample (columns `unstranded`, `stranded_first`, `stranded_second`, `tpm_unstranded`, `fpkm_unstranded`, ...).
- Clinical data come as case records (vital status, days to death, follow-ups, stage, grade) that have to be combined into one survival time.
- Open tier: gene-level counts and clinical data; controlled tier (dbGaP authorisation): reads/BAMs and germline data.

items.gloss_md: NCBI's public repository of functional genomics data; a study is a series (GSE), a platform a GPL, a sample a GSM.
items.body_md:
- URL: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/>; open access, no registration.
- Accession types: **GSE** series (a study), **GPL** platform (the array or sequencer, with the probe-to-gene table), **GSM** sample, GDS curated data set.
- Downloads: the *series matrix* (processed values plus sample characteristics such as survival) and supplementary files (e.g. raw count tables, CEL files).
- Survival, if deposited, sits in the free-text `characteristics` lines, in units chosen by the depositor (months, years or days).

items.gloss_md: The tab-separated text file of a GEO series: metadata lines starting with `!`, then the expression block between `!series_matrix_table_begin` and `!series_matrix_table_end`.
items.body_md:
- First column: probe (or gene) identifiers; one further column per sample (GSM).
- Sample annotation lines (`!Sample_characteristics_ch1`) carry `key: value` pairs, e.g. `os time: 23.4`, `os event: 1`; the keys differ between series.
- Probe ids are mapped to gene symbols with the platform table (GPL); several probes per gene are collapsed, e.g. by keeping the probe with the highest mean.
- Raw counts of RNA-seq series are usually not in the matrix but in a supplementary file.

items.gloss_md: The GEO record of a measurement platform; for an array it holds the annotation table that maps each probe to a gene.
items.body_md: - A custom or manufacturer-specific probe set maps to gene symbols with its own ambiguities, so a score that needs a particular gene may find no probe for it.

items.gloss_md: EMBL-EBI's functional genomics archive, now served inside BioStudies; accessions look like E-MTAB-6134.
items.body_md:
- URL: <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress>; open access.
- A study has processed data files (e.g. `ProcessedExpression.tsv`), raw files (e.g. CEL) and an **SDRF** file (Sample and Data Relationship Format) with one row per sample: the clinical annotation such as OS, DFS, grade, TNM, margin and centre.

items.gloss_md: EMBL-EBI/CRG archive for personally identifiable genomic data; access to every data set is granted by its own data access committee.
items.body_md:
- URL: <https://ega-archive.org>; study accessions `EGAS...`, data sets `EGAD...`.
- Controlled access: an application with a project description and an institutional signature goes to the data access committee (DAC) of the data owner.

items.label_md: ICGC Data Portal and ICGC ARGO
items.gloss_md: The portals of the International Cancer Genome Consortium; the former Data Coordination Centre (dcc.icgc.org, ICGC 25K) is succeeded by ICGC ARGO.
items.body_md:
- URLs: <https://dcc.icgc.org/> (ICGC 25K data release) and <https://www.icgc-argo.org/>; older download addresses in papers and scripts redirect or no longer work.
- Holds the donor clinical data, including survival, of PACA-AU and PACA-CA; the sequences themselves are in EGA under controlled access.
- Consequence: expression matrix and survival table of an ICGC cohort live in different places and must be joined by donor id.

items.label_md: TOIL recompute of TCGA and GTEx
items.gloss_md: Re-processing of TCGA and GTEx RNA-seq through one pipeline (Vivian et al. 2017, Toil workflow engine), so that tumour and normal samples are comparable.
items.body_md:
- TCGA and GTEx originally used different aligners, annotations and quantification tools; those differences are larger than many biological effects.
- The recompute is served on the TOIL hub of UCSC Xena; TCGA and GTEx matrices then share the same genes (58,581 symbols).
- It removes pipeline differences, not differences in origin: TCGA tumours were frozen at surgery, GTEx tissue was taken after death, with other inclusion criteria and protocols.

items.gloss_md: The pancreatic adenocarcinoma project of The Cancer Genome Atlas: bulk RNA-seq of resected tumours with overall survival, open via GDC and UCSC Xena (TCGA 2017, Cancer Cell).
items.body_md:
- Samples: 185 in the Xena expression matrix, 178 of them primary tumours; the definitive paper (Raphael et al., TCGA Research Network 2017) analyses 150 histopathologically curated PDAC.
- Platform: Illumina RNA-seq, GDC STAR quantification against GENCODE v36 (60,660 Ensembl ids, 59,427 gene symbols).
- Endpoints: OS and PFI from the TCGA-CDR, plus age, sex and AJCC stage; mostly resected patients of similar stage, short follow-up with more events than censorings.
- Access: open.
- Caveat: the project name is not a diagnosis; normal/pseudo-normal and neuroendocrine samples must be removed first (Peran 2018).

items.gloss_md: The list of 150 histopathologically confirmed PDAC that the TCGA 2017 paper analysed; it absorbs the curation of Peran et al. 2018 (Clin Cancer Res).
items.body_md:
- Peran et al. 2018 named 33 TCGA-PAAD profiles that are not PDAC: 16 normal or pseudo-normal pancreas and 17 other tumours, among them eight neuroendocrine tumours.
- Why it matters: a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour has a different transcriptome and survival measured in years; a few of them make every neuroendocrine-vs-ductal gene look prognostic, and cross-validation does not repair it (a confounder, not a leak).
- TCGA 2017 split the 150 at the median ABSOLUTE purity (33 %) into 76 high-purity and 74 low-purity tumours for a two-stage analysis.

items.gloss_md: The pan-cancer survival table of Liu et al. 2018 (Cell) that defines OS, DSS, DFI and PFI uniformly for all TCGA patients and rates their reliability.
items.body_md:
- 10,496 samples with OS, DSS (disease-specific survival), DFI (disease-free interval) and PFI (progression-free interval), each with time and event.
- Recommended over the per-project clinical files because the endpoints are defined the same way across cancer types and the paper says which are reliable for which cancer.
- On Xena as `Survival_SupplementalTable_S1_20171025_xena_sp`.

items.label_md: ICGC PACA-AU (Australian Pancreatic Cancer Genome Initiative)
items.gloss_md: The Australian ICGC pancreatic cancer cohort behind Bailey et al. 2016 (Nature): arrays open in GEO, RNA-seq controlled in EGA, survival in the ICGC portal.
items.body_md:
- 456 genomically characterised tumours; expression by RNA-seq for 96 tumours (EGA EGAS00001000154, controlled) and by Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 arrays for 232 tumours, 91 of which are open as GSE36924 (Biankin et al. 2012, Nature).
- Endpoint: OS, held in the ICGC portal rather than in the sequence archives.
- pdacR ships a joined PACA-AU RNA-seq matrix of 92 samples with survival.
- The standard external validation of PDAC signatures; PurIST validated on it and PAMG used 267 resected ICGC patients.

items.gloss_md: The Canadian ICGC cohort of Chan-Seng-Yue et al. 2020 (Nature Genetics): whole-genome and RNA sequencing of laser-capture-microdissected tumour epithelium.
items.body_md:
- 330 tumours from 314 patients with whole-genome sequencing after LCM; 248 also have RNA-seq, on which the paper derived its five expression classes.
- Access: controlled (EGA EGAS00001002543); pdacR contains an expression matrix of 262 PACA-CA samples with survival built from the ICGC portal.
- Microdissected epithelium, so tumour content is much higher than in bulk cohorts; a score dominated by stromal or immune genes behaves differently here.
- The same programme produced single-cell data used together with Peng 2019.

items.gloss_md: The proteogenomic PDAC cohort of the NCI Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (Cao et al. 2021, Cell): RNA-seq, proteome, phosphoproteome and glycoproteome of the same tumours.
items.body_md:
- 245 open-access STAR gene-count files for 168 cases at the GDC (GENCODE v36), primary tumour and normal samples mixed; one primary tumour per case gives 161 tumours, 159 with OS and 128 deaths.
- Survival has to be assembled from GDC case records (vital status, days to death, follow-ups); normal samples must be removed first.
- Unique strength: protein data on the same tumours, so an RNA score can be checked at the protein level (the proteomic data are a separate download, at the CPTAC Proteomic Data Commons).
- Access: open for expression and clinical data under the GDC data use policy.

items.gloss_md: RNA-seq gene counts of 51 resected PDAC with overall survival in days (Kirby et al. 2016, Molecular Oncology), open in GEO.
items.body_md:
- 51 primary PDAC, OS for all with 45 deaths; age, sex and TNM.
- Raw counts (`GSE79668_51_tumors_sharedgenecounts.txt.gz`, gene ids `SYMBOL_ENSG`), so normalisation is under the analyst's control.
- The only small cohort measured by RNA-seq, so a TCGA-trained model applies without cross-platform translation.
- Caveats: survival in days (others in months); 51 patients are confirmation, not evidence.

items.gloss_md: 309 FFPE resected PDAC from four European centres on Affymetrix HG-U219 with OS and DFS (Puleo et al. 2018, Gastroenterology), open in ArrayExpress.
items.body_md:
- The largest open PDAC cohort with survival: OS for 288 patients (181 deaths in the deposit), DFS, grade, TNM, margin, centre and the Puleo subtype call.
- FFPE is what pathology archives hold and what a trial would use; four centres give a realistic batch structure.
- Caveats: the subtype calls are the authors' own; FFPE RNA is degraded, so intensities compress.
- Also the discovery cohort of Hilmi 2021 (distant recurrence) and a validation series of PAMG (308 resection specimens).

items.gloss_md: The custom Agilent array series behind the classical/basal-like and normal/activated stroma subtypes (Moffitt et al. 2015, Nature Genetics).
items.body_md:
- 357 arrays: 145 primary tumours (125 with OS in months, 84 deaths), 61 metastases, 46 normal pancreata, 88 distant-site normal tissues and 17 cell lines; platform GPL20769 (summarised to 19,749 gene symbols).
- The mix of tumours, metastases, normal tissues and cell lines is what made the virtual microdissection (NMF) possible.
- Carries both the tumour and the stroma subtype calls in its sample table; 106 of its primaries were already in GSE21501.
- A PurIST training cohort; caveats: two-colour ratio scale and author-assigned labels.

items.gloss_md: Agilent 4x44K two-colour arrays of 132 PDAC samples against a common reference with OS (Stratford et al. 2010, PLoS Medicine).
items.body_md:
- 121 primary tumours; OS in months for 102 patients with 66 deaths; platform GPL4133.
- Every value is a ratio against a common reference sample, not an absolute intensity, so a score on absolute levels must be re-standardised; a rank-based score is unaffected.
- Overlaps GSE71729 (106 primaries).

items.gloss_md: Affymetrix HuGene 1.0 ST profiles of 69 PDAC and 61 adjacent non-tumour tissues from an NCI group (Yang et al. 2016, Cancer Research).
items.body_md:
- OS in months for 66 tumours with 50 deaths; platform GPL6244; the best gene coverage of the array cohorts.
- The external validation most often used by the PDAC immune-signature papers (IRGPI among them), so the place to compare with them directly.
- Adjacent non-tumour tissue handled like the tumours is a better normal reference than GTEx.
- Overlaps GSE183795 (same group and platform): never count the two as independent validations.

items.gloss_md: 244 Affymetrix HuGene 1.0 ST profiles (139 PDAC, 102 adjacent non-tumour, 3 normal) from the same NCI group and platform as GSE62452, with grade, stage and margin.
items.body_md:
- The largest GEO cohort with survival here (OS for 189 samples, 127 deaths); survival is also attached to non-tumour samples of the same patients, so select tumours first and deduplicate by patient.
- Overlaps GSE62452; the accessions look unrelated and papers using GSE62452 rarely mention it.

items.gloss_md: 80 resected PDAC on Affymetrix HG-U219 (GPL13667) with OS in years.
items.body_md:
- OS for 79 patients with 57 deaths, deposited in years (`os.year`, `death`).
- Same platform as E-MTAB-6134, so a cheap technical replicate: a score that behaves very differently on the two has a platform problem rather than a biology problem.

items.gloss_md: 63 PDAC on a custom Rosetta/Merck Affymetrix array (GPL15048) with OS in months and stage (Chen et al. 2015, PLoS One).
items.body_md:
- OS for all 63 with 42 deaths.
- One of the four validation cohorts of Li 2022, so useful for reproducing a published comparison on the same data.
- Custom array: probe-to-gene mapping has its own ambiguities.

items.gloss_md: RNA-seq (counts and TPM) of 289 FFPE primary and metastatic PDAC, 218 primaries, without follow-up in GEO.
items.body_md:
- No survival: expression questions only.
- The largest set of primary and metastatic PDAC on one platform; the study compared primaries that metastasised to the liver with those that went to the lung.
- Trap: separating primaries from metastases is a tissue-origin question (a liver metastasis is surrounded by hepatocytes) and clinically useless; predicting later spread needs follow-up; detecting an occult deposit in a 'resectable' patient needs pre-treatment biopsies and a reference standard, which no public data set provides.

items.gloss_md: The open array half of ICGC PACA-AU: 91 PDAC on Illumina HumanHT-12 v4 as non-normalised intensities, no survival in GEO.
items.body_md:
- Part of the 232-sample array arm analysed by Bailey 2016; first published by Biankin et al. 2012 (Nature).
- Survival only via the ICGC clinical data; pdacR carries a joined RNA-seq version of PACA-AU instead.
- Use: expression questions (does a gene set behave the same on a third array platform, can the Bailey classes be recovered).

items.gloss_md: The discovery data of the Collisson subtypes (Nature Medicine 2011): 62 samples, 27 of them microdissected primary PDAC, plus human and mouse cell lines, on Affymetrix U133 Plus 2.0.
items.body_md:
- About 20,000 genes; OS reported in the paper.
- Microdissection in the discovery cohort is one reason the scheme does not move into routine bulk material.

items.gloss_md: LCM RNA-seq of PDAC epithelium and stroma (Maurer et al. 2019, Gut): 204 samples from 122 patients, 60 matched epithelium/stroma pairs, 110 stromal profiles.
items.body_md:
- Libraries by Ovation RNA-Seq V2, about 30 million 100 bp single-end reads.
- Training data of ADVOCATE, which estimates epithelial and stromal fractions and compartment profiles from bulk.

items.gloss_md: Transcriptomes of 76 patient-derived xenografts of the French PaCaOmics programme, from which Nicolle et al. 2020 derived PAMG by independent component analysis.
items.body_md:
- Open in ArrayExpress.
- Xenografts lose the human stroma (it is replaced by mouse stroma), so human reads reflect the tumour cells: a way around low purity.
- PAMG was then validated in ICGC (267 resected), Puleo E-MTAB-6134 (308), BACAP (60 biopsies) and COMPASS (28 biopsies).

items.gloss_md: The authors' own prospective French cohort used by Nicolle 2020 to validate PAMG on 60 fine-needle biopsies, 47 of them advanced and with survival; not public.
items.body_md:
- Shows that PAMG works on biopsies, the material available before treatment.
- No public accession.

items.gloss_md: Biopsies of advanced PDAC sequenced after laser capture microdissection in the Canadian COMPASS trial (Aung et al. 2018), with treatment response.
items.body_md:
- 49 RNA-seq samples in the PurIST validation (treatment response); 28 COMPASS biopsies under mFOLFIRINOX in the PAMG validation.
- One of the few cohorts that link pre-treatment biopsies to response, so used to show that basal-like tumours respond poorly to FOLFIRINOX.

items.gloss_md: RNA-seq of metastatic PDAC biopsies (Aguirre and colleagues, Dana-Farber) that was one of the three PurIST training sets; not public.
items.body_md:
- PurIST was trained on GSE71729, TCGA-PAAD and the Aguirre biopsies (321 training labels).
- No public accession, so PurIST's training cannot be fully reproduced.

items.gloss_md: The in-house series of the Yeh lab deposited with PurIST (Rashid et al. 2020): RNA-seq of matched bulk, fine-needle aspirate, FFPE and xenograft samples (GSE131050) and NanoString data (GSE131051).
items.body_md:
- GSE131050: 47 matched FNA vs bulk pairs plus 5 matched FFPE/FNA/bulk sets, a sample-type check.
- GSE131051: 51 samples on NanoString, the platform check of the NanoString version of PurIST.
- Shows that the classifier gives the same call on different material from the same tumour.

items.gloss_md: RNA-seq of 66 PDAC from the phase Ib trial of Nywening and colleagues (Linehan group, Washington University), used to validate PurIST with treatment response.
items.body_md: - Listed by PurIST as a validation cohort for subtype and treatment response.

items.gloss_md: 149 resected PDAC from Beaujon hospital (Paris) on 3' RNA-seq (QuantSeq) that validated Hilmi 2021's distant-recurrence finding; no public accession.
items.body_md: - Discovery was E-MTAB-6134 (381 patients, 309 profiled); validation 149 (133 with relapse data).

items.gloss_md: 101 PDAC from Ruijin hospital (Shanghai) measured by qRT-PCR of 18 genes, with immunohistochemistry on 81 and OS/DFS; not public.
items.body_md: - An example of a signature validated only on a small targeted panel in a non-public cohort.

items.gloss_md: Healthy pancreas RNA-seq of deceased donors from the Genotype-Tissue Expression project (GTEx Consortium 2020, Science), the normal reference for tumour-vs-normal comparisons.
items.body_md:
- No endpoints: the donors have no tumour-related course.
- Comparable with TCGA only after the TOIL recompute through one pipeline.
- Caveat: healthy pancreas is about 98 % exocrine tissue whose acinar cells make almost only digestive enzymes; a PDAC nodule has hardly any acini, so nearly every non-acinar gene looks 'up' in the tumour. The direction is usable as a sign, the magnitude is not an effect size.

items.label_md: Peng et al. 2019 PDAC single-cell atlas
items.gloss_md: Single-cell RNA-seq of primary PDAC and control pancreas (Peng et al. 2019, Cell Research).
items.body_md:
- About 24 primary PDAC and 11 control pancreases, roughly 57,000 cells; raw data in the Genome Sequence Archive of the China National Center for Bioinformation (accession CRA001160).
- Describes intra-tumoural heterogeneity and two ductal populations (normal-like and malignant).

items.label_md: Public PDAC single-cell cohorts and the Loveless 2025 atlas
items.gloss_md: All public PDAC scRNA-seq cohorts have fewer than 50 patients; the merged atlas of Loveless et al. 2025 (Zenodo 14199536) pools 229 samples in a 33 GB Seurat object.
items.body_md: - Single-cell cohorts answer which cell type expresses a gene, not how long a patient lives: too few patients for a survival model.

items.gloss_md: The stable public identifier a repository gives a data set, which a paper cites so that others can find the data.
items.body_md:
- Prefixes tell the repository: GSE/GSM/GPL (GEO), E-MTAB (ArrayExpress), EGAS/EGAD (EGA), CRA (Genome Sequence Archive, China), Zenodo DOIs.
- A paper without an accession usually means the data are not public (e.g. BACAP, the Aguirre biopsies, the Beaujon and Ruijin cohorts).

items.gloss_md: Open data can be downloaded by anyone; controlled data (identifiable genomic data) are released only after an approved application.
items.body_md:
- Open: GEO, ArrayExpress, GDC gene-level counts and clinical data, UCSC Xena.
- Controlled: raw reads and germline data at the GDC (dbGaP authorisation) and every EGA data set, e.g. the RNA-seq of ICGC PACA-AU and PACA-CA.
- An application needs a project description, data security commitments and an institutional signature; processed matrices are sometimes open even when raw sequences are not.

items.gloss_md: The body of the data owner that reviews applications for controlled-access data and sets the conditions of use.
items.body_md:
- Each EGA data set names its DAC; for TCGA/GDC controlled data the NIH dbGaP process plays this role.
- Approval usually binds the data to a named project, institution and secure storage, and forbids redistribution.

items.gloss_md: Re-processing all samples of a resource from raw reads with one fixed pipeline and annotation, so that values are comparable across projects.
items.body_md:
- Examples: the GDC harmonisation (STAR, GRCh38, GENCODE v36 for TCGA and CPTAC) and the TOIL recompute of TCGA plus GTEx.
- Harmonisation removes pipeline differences, not differences in tissue handling, protocols or populations (batch effects of origin remain).

items.gloss_md: The per-sample RNA-seq quantification of the GDC: a tab-separated table of genes (GENCODE v36 Ensembl ids) with raw counts and derived TPM and FPKM columns.
items.body_md:
- Columns: `gene_id`, `gene_name`, `gene_type`, `unstranded`, `stranded_first`, `stranded_second`, `tpm_unstranded`, `fpkm_unstranded`, `fpkm_uq_unstranded`.
- One file per sample, linked to cases via the file list; reading 161 CPTAC-3 files takes about 10 s, so the matrix is worth caching.

items.gloss_md: The gene annotation release used by the GDC for its harmonised RNA-seq (60,660 genes with Ensembl ids), and therefore by TCGA-PAAD and CPTAC-3 counts.
items.body_md:
- Gene ids carry a version suffix (`ENSG00000141510.18`); map to HGNC symbols with the annotation or a Xena probemap.
- Several Ensembl ids can share one symbol (59,427 symbols from 60,660 ids), so rows have to be collapsed.

items.gloss_md: The mapping file UCSC Xena ships next to its matrices that links each row identifier (probe or Ensembl id) to a gene symbol and position.
items.body_md:
- For TCGA-PAAD from the GDC hub: `gencode.v36.annotation.gtf.gene.probemap`.
- Needed because Xena matrices are indexed by Ensembl id, not by symbol.

items.gloss_md: The identifier of a TCGA aliquot, e.g. `TCGA-2J-AAB1-01A`: project, tissue source site, participant, then a sample-type code.
items.body_md:
- The first 12 characters identify the patient, so they deduplicate samples per patient.
- Different sources write it differently (`TCGA.2J.AAB1.01` vs `TCGA-2J-AAB1-01A`), which breaks naive joins.

items.label_md: Adjacent non-tumour tissue as normal reference
items.gloss_md: Pancreas next to the tumour from the same resection, used instead of healthy-donor tissue as the normal reference.
items.body_md:
- Advantage: handled, stored and measured like the tumour, so fewer batch effects than GTEx.
- Not healthy: it can carry pancreatitis, atrophy, PanIN or tumour cells and is altered by the nearby tumour (field effect).

items.gloss_md: Survival times are deposited in months (most cohorts), years (GSE85916) or days (GSE79668, GDC case records); pooling them unconverted silently corrupts a model.
items.body_md:
- A year counted as a month makes those patients look as if they died 12 times sooner.
- Check: compare the median follow-up per cohort before fitting; PDAC median OS after resection is roughly 1.5-2 years.

items.gloss_md: Two accessions that share patients (e.g. GSE62452 and GSE183795, GSE21501 and GSE71729) are one cohort, not two independent validations.
items.body_md:
- Easy to miss because the accessions look unrelated.
- Detect by correlating every sample of one series with every sample of the other on the same genes: true duplicates stand out as best matches with very high correlation; choose the threshold without looking at survival.

items.gloss_md: On two-colour arrays against a common reference (GSE21501, GSE71729) every value is a log ratio to the reference sample, not an absolute intensity.
items.body_md:
- Removes some technical variation, but the scale differs from all one-colour platforms.
- A score built on absolute levels must be re-standardised gene by gene; a rank-based within-sample score such as PurIST's gene pairs is unaffected.

items.label_md: What a prognostic training cohort must offer
items.gloss_md: Expression from primary tumours, a censored survival endpoint and clinical variables known at prediction time, all for the same patients.
items.body_md:
- Not a metastasis, cell line or xenograft; without an event indicator a cohort is useless for a prognostic model; and the question is always whether expression adds to the pathology report.
- Small cohorts: at about 66 patients a C-index has a confidence interval of roughly ±0.08, so differences below about 0.1 cannot be resolved one cohort at a time.
